title: Infection Spread Simulation IV — Pending Death
prompt:
This standalone problem is the fourth exercise in the Infection Spread Simulation series. Use `HEALTHY = 0`, `INFECTED = 1`, `IMMUNE = 2`, and `DEAD = 3`.

Implement `simulate_pending_death(grid, infectious_days, death_threshold, infection_threshold=1, directions=DIR4)`. Infection and recovery timers follow Part III. If an infected cell has at least `death_threshold` infected neighbors on any sick day, permanently mark it doomed. The infection day counts for a newly infected cell: use the same start-of-day neighbor count that infected it to decide whether it is immediately doomed. A doomed cell stays infected until its normal recovery day and then becomes dead instead of immune. Dead and immune cells never change or transmit.

Return `(days_to_stability, dead_count, final_grid)` when no infected cells remain. You may assume the grid is non-empty and rectangular, every cell is a known state, and the timer and threshold values are positive integers; you do not need to validate these inputs. Do not mutate the input. You do not need to implement Parts I–III.
